headline: Compressed dynamic indexes for k-mers, syncmers, and pangenome graphs
label: Space Efficient Sequence Indexing
summary: Recent preprints target space and time efficiency for k-mer, syncmer, and pangenome path indexing across genome collections.
synthesis: The common thread is space-efficient indexing over sequence substrings and graphs. Fast Iteration of Spaced k-mers treats k-mers as a ubiquitous indexing primitive and addresses spaced k-mer design. A run-length-compressed doubly-linked skiplist for dynamic GBWTs supports time- and space-efficient pangenome path search over syncmer graphs. Together these two preprints pair spaced k-mers and syncmers as index primitives with compressed dynamic structures for pangenome queries, which is the new element. Scalable computation of ultrabubbles in pangenomes by orienting bidirected graphs describes a linear-time orientation algorithm that computes ultrabubbles via weak superbubbles, reporting up to 25x speedup over vg. A separate preprint on phylogenetic compression of bacterial genome collections shows the problem is NP-hard in general but polynomial-time optimal under the Infinite Sites Model. The items do not compare these approaches directly.
